0.8.0 turns rust-doctor from a scanner you run into a loop that runs itself: on the lines an agent just wrote, on the index a commit is about to record, on the pull request CI judges. The catalog grows from 62 rules to 142, the score moves to `core-v5`, and the report schema from 17 to 23. Read [Breaking changes](#breaking-changes) before upgrading a gate, the Action or an installed hook.

## Breaking changes

### The catalog more than doubles and the score is `core-v5`

Eighty rules join the catalog ([66bffe9](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/66bffe9), [ac221f2](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/ac221f2), [8782b39](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/8782b39)):

| Producer | 0.7.0 | 0.8.0 |
|---|---:|---:|
| `clippy::*` | 37 | 104 |
| `rust_doctor::source::*` | 2 | 11 |
| `rust_doctor::cargo::*` | 11 | 13 |
| `rust_doctor::structure::*` | 9 | 9 |
| `rust_doctor::repo::*` | 3 | 5 |

The scan used to open with `-A clippy::all`, which silenced every lint Clippy denies by default: a workspace holding `if a == a` scored a clean correctness dimension while plain `cargo clippy` refused it. The 64 members of `clippy::correctness` that `std` code can trigger are now catalogued at `P1`. The other sixteen are listed under [New rules](#new-rules).

`core-v5` changes one thing in the density penalty: a rule counted against the workspace, such as a duplicate major version, charges what members claim once per member mean instead of adding it up, so a workspace lands between its worst and best member ([53ec6ee](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/53ec6ee)). Added up, paneflow's workspace scored 46 under members at 73 and above.

The corpus moves both ways. The repository pass now runs on it, since its subjects are measured as git clones rather than bare trees ([dcc9d07](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/dcc9d07)):

| Workspace | 0.7.0 | 0.8.0 | What moved it |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| anyhow | 88 | 73 | 57 sites of `clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks` |
| bytes | 89 | 82 | 96 sites of `clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks` |
| mdr | 88 | 65 | `repo::secret_in_build_step`, which the bare tree hid |
| vibesql | 73 | 58 | `blocking_call_in_async`, `sql_built_from_format`, `unused_dependency` |
| ostendo | 84 | 79 | `unused_dependency`, `test_only_dependency` |
| artifexprocal | 79 | 90 | `core-v5`, same findings |

The twelve other pinned repositories did not move. The healthy median now sits 8 points above the agent one, against 6.5 under 0.7.0.

**Upgrade path.** Re-measure a CI threshold rather than keeping the old one:

```bash
rust-doctor . --yes --json | jq '{value: .audit.score.value, model: .audit.score.model}'
```

A `--scope baseline` gate carries no threshold, and a rule you do not want is switched off in `rust-doctor.toml` or with `--rule clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks=off`.

### `schema_version` is 23

Six bumps in one release, each additive to a reader that ignores unknown members:

- An uncatalogued compiler warning is published with `unscored: "uncatalogued"`, listed last under "Compiler notes (not scored)", and weighs on neither the score nor the gate, so one `unused_imports` no longer voids the score. A partial score names its causes in `audit.score.reasons`, and `toolchain.rust_doctor` names the binary.
- A catalogued rule the installed Clippy does not know is published with `not_evaluated: "unknown-to-toolchain"` instead of failing the scan. `toolchain.removed_lint_flags` lists the lint-level tokens stripped from `RUSTFLAGS`, `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS` and `[build] rustflags`.
- `suppressions[]`, `scan.ignored`, `scan.excluded_generated` and `audit.packages[]`, which scores every scanned member on its own lines.
- `scan.advisory_db`, the `advisory-db-missing` reason, and the `contextual` scope mode.
- `timings` under `--timings`, and the rule descriptors' `diff_scope`, `requires`, `title` and `not_a_defect_when`.

**Upgrade path.** Anything asserting `schema_version == 17` asserts `23`; the frozen v7 archive still projects. In the Rust library the report structs gain public fields, which breaks a struct literal, and `ScopeMode` gains `Lines` and `Contextual`, which breaks an exhaustive `match`.

### The Action no longer fails a push on findings

`uses: arthjean/rust-doctor@v0` now fails the job on the gate (exit 1) only on a `pull_request` event. A push, a schedule or a manual run is a health snapshot: the job summary still renders the score and the findings, the outputs are still set, and the step exits 0. A scan that could not run (exit 2) still fails on every event ([2d677d1](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/2d677d1)). The workflow `rust-doctor ci install` writes applies the same rule.

**Upgrade path.** To keep failing pushes on findings, read the `exit-code` output in a step of your own.

### The pre-commit hook blocks on warnings

The hook runs its staged scan with `--blocking warning`, as the end-of-turn hook does, so a hook with no configuration refuses a commit that adds a finding. A scan that fails (exit 2) and a missing `rust-doctor` on `PATH` both let the commit through, saying on stderr that it was not judged ([b33ae22](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/b33ae22)).

**Upgrade path.** An installed hook keeps its old body until rewritten:

```bash
rust-doctor hook install git --update
```

An outdated hook is reported as outdated, never as installed.

### A scan publishes no score it did not compute

A build Cargo refused before building, a workspace with no member Clippy linted, and a run a signal stopped now publish a null score instead of a hundred over code nothing linted ([d9a4bcf](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/d9a4bcf)). A first `SIGINT`, `SIGTERM` or `SIGHUP` kills every child's process group and exits 130 with one failed report; a second within 500 ms is the same delivery, a later one exits at once. A missing or unreadable `--advisory-db` exits 2, with `/dev/null` as the off switch, and the installers refuse a missing path with exit 2 instead of creating directories.

## New rules

The 80 rules are published by `rust-doctor rules list` and by [rust-doctor.com/rules](https://rust-doctor.com/rules). Beyond the correctness pack:

- Unsafe code: `clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks`, `clippy::missing_transmute_annotations`, `clippy::crosspointer_transmute`.
- Async services: `blocking_call_in_async`, which follows a call into a synchronous helper of the same file four levels deep, `block_on_in_async`, `block_in_place_on_current_thread`, and `unchecked_http_status` for a reqwest body read without a status check.
- Injection and auth: `sql_built_from_format` (`format!`, `write!`, `QueryBuilder::push`, `diesel::dsl::sql`, `sea_orm::Statement::from_string`), `permissive_cors`, `insecure_auth_cookie`, `disabled_jwt_validation`, `secret_env_fallback`.
- Dependencies: `vulnerable_dependency` and `unmaintained_dependency` judge `Cargo.lock` against a local RustSec database, the one `--advisory-db` names or the one `cargo audit` or `cargo deny` left. The tool never fetches one; without it both rules are published as not evaluated and the score keeps its authority.
- Repository: `ignored_lockfile`, and `secret_in_build_step` for a CI step compiling with secrets in its environment.

A crate rule is gated on each member's resolved version of the crate it judges, and every rule now publishes a title and the case that is not a defect.

## The agent loop

- `--scope lines` keeps a finding only where its span meets a changed range. `--scope contextual` judges a rule whose cause can sit above its site by the function around it, so an `.await` added under a held lock is reported. `--staged` judges the index materialized into its own tree, `--include-untracked` adds untracked files whole ([abf595c](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/abf595c), [ac221f2](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/ac221f2)).
- `--base` is optional: the scopes resolve the default branch (`origin/HEAD`, `origin/main`, `origin/master`, `main`, `master`, or `HEAD` on it), and fail with `base-undetected` or `shallow-clone` and the remedy.
- `hook install git` writes a pre-commit hook that follows `core.hooksPath`, cargo-husky, lefthook or another hook manager. `hook install claude|cursor` merges one end-of-turn entry that rescans the turn's lines, and stays silent on an aborted, failed or already resubmitted turn. `setup` installs the skill and the hooks for the agents it detects, and `skill install` takes `--agent claude|codex|cursor|all`, `--update` and `--dry-run`.
- A dependency finding is anchored at its manifest key, so a staged `foo = "*"` fails the pre-commit hook. A clone family stays in scope when any member changed. The delta pairs findings through Git renames and hunk line maps, so a refactor no longer reports what it moved as introduced ([8782b39](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/8782b39)).
- A path with no workspace above it scans the one below it, `src-tauri/` for instance, or refuses several as `ambiguous-workspace`.

## Precision controls

- `rust-doctor.toml` accepts `[ignore] paths` and `[[overrides]]` tables whose `paths` globs set `rules` and `categories` levels. The last override covering a path wins, and `--rule` or `--category` still wins over the file ([51440b7](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/51440b7)).
- `// rust-doctor: allow(<id>) -- <reason>` silences a native finding on its line or the next, and `# rust-doctor: allow(<id>)` above a key does the same in `Cargo.toml` and `.cargo/config.toml`. `suppressions[]` reports each one as applied, unused, missing-reason, use-expect or unknown-rule.
- Files `.gitattributes` marks `linguist-generated` or `linguist-vendored`, and files opening on a generator header, leave every producer and the measured lines ([0cf2009](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/0cf2009)).
- `--package <NAME>` scans and scores one member, repeatable.

## CI

- `rust-doctor ci install` writes `.github/workflows/rust-doctor.yml` at the git root, pinned to the binary's version and toolchain, never over a file it did not write; `--update` rewrites its own and `--comment` adds the sticky comment ([5631411](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/5631411), [a195d9b](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/a195d9b)).
- `action.yml` is a composite Action publishing `score`, `authoritative`, `introduced`, `fixed` and `exit-code`, a job summary, the report artifact, and one sticky comment from the scan job (`comment`, true by default; `comment-on-clean: false` keeps a clean pull request free of a new one). It restores and saves Cargo's build with rust-cache, on failure too (`cache: false` turns it off), fetches the base of a shallow pull request checkout itself, and pins every third-party action to a commit.
- `rust-doctor report markdown <FILE>` renders a saved JSON report for a job summary or a comment. A failed scan renders its errors by stage and code, says no finding was collected, and names `fetch-depth: 0` when the checkout lacked the base's history, instead of "No finding.".

## Reading the report

- `rust-doctor rules explain <ID>` explains a rule, and `rust-doctor why <PATH:LINE>` explains a site and how to silence it, from a fresh scan or a saved `--report`.
- `--warning-exit-code <CODE>` (3 to 125) marks a run whose gate passed with a finding `--blocking warning` would block.
- `--timings`, and `--verbose` outside `--json`, publish each phase in milliseconds. The passes now overlap, Clippy on its own thread beside the native passes: a warm full scan of this repository went from 577 ms to 379 ms, median of seven release runs ([8782b39](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/8782b39)).
- A `--scope baseline` run reads its base side from a cache under the target directory and spawns no Cargo process for an unchanged base; `RUST_DOCTOR_NO_CACHE=1` turns it off.
- `--max-duration <SECONDS>` bounds the whole run, killing every process it started, build scripts included. The report keeps what was collected and exits 2.
- The default report lists every scored rule at the terminal's live width, then `COLUMNS`, then 80, labels non-production sites, and says why a report is empty or unscored. `--yes`, `CI` set to anything but `false` or `0`, and 26 agent, hook and CI markers get final output only, with no count-up and no rewritten progress line. An empty `NO_COLOR` keeps color, as no-color.org prescribes.

## Fixes

- A failed scan published "Clippy exited with status 101" and nothing else. It now ends with the last kilobyte of Cargo's stderr, color escapes removed and scrubbed of the workspace root, the target directory, `CARGO_HOME`, `RUSTUP_HOME` and `HOME` ([8cce13d](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/8cce13d), [bcb2b48](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/bcb2b48)). Every other message keeps only the last directory and file name of an absolute path ([30f9031](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/30f9031)).
- No detected credential reaches a screen: code frames mask every credential the repository pass matches, a PEM body opened above the window and a secret fallback literal included, and a Clippy suggestion that would reprint one is withheld, across the terminal, the viewer, the handoff prompt, `why` and `report markdown` ([ac221f2](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/ac221f2), [062bbf6](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/062bbf6), [30f9031](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/30f9031), [953bf85](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/953bf85)).
- The repository pass runs on the tree a `--staged` or baseline scan judges, so the pre-commit hook no longer lets a staged key through and a no-op branch no longer introduces every repository finding ([921fb6c](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/921fb6c)). Outside git it walks the files present instead of finding nothing ([cebb1cf](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/cebb1cf)).
- A scan puts `Cargo.lock` back as it was, so two scans of a lockless crate agree and the tree stays byte-identical ([d9a4bcf](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/d9a4bcf)).
- Incremental compilation is pinned off for the Clippy run: it counted a macro-expanded site once per expansion, 41 locally against 31 under rust-cache ([7e17e6f](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/7e17e6f)).
- The native rules hold their verdict: a glob import no longer erases a name's provenance, a numeric parameter is not injectable text, the shell rule reads ksh, cmd, PowerShell and absolute shell paths, the credential rule requires a key body and vetoes placeholders, and `unchecked_http_status` accepts `and_then(Response::error_for_status)` ([1f6f2cb](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/1f6f2cb), [d8b5180](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/d8b5180), [42d5b51](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/42d5b51), [0b9698b](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/0b9698b)). Nine not-a-defect checks were rewritten against Clippy 1.97.1 ([4dcf83a](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/4dcf83a)).
- A dimension holding the score under its ceiling is named as the cause rather than the ceiling ([e966895](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/e966895)), and the production file count leaves out the test files the detectors read ([001abc1](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/001abc1)).
- rust-doctor opens no network connection, but Cargo downloads a missing dependency: the help now says so and names `CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true`. Every git call runs with Git LFS's smudge filter off, so a snapshot never downloads a pointer file ([b33ae22](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/b33ae22)).

## Internal

More than half of the release's 72 commits change nothing observable outside the repository: the PRD records and their certifications, now dropped from `tasks/`, and the test harness. `tests/e2e/` drives the release binary in sealed copies across every scan argument, scope, subcommand, failure mode and terminal scenario, replays the packed npm launcher and the Action's bash steps, and holds every open defect as a `test.failing` row ([7c66993](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/7c66993), [dd699da](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/dd699da), [395ea55](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/395ea55)). The corpus is measured on git clones in a job graph that replaces `e2e-corpus.yml` and runs weekly ([dcc9d07](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/dcc9d07)). Every fixed false positive of a native rule is a regression seed `cargo test` replays. The rest are CI stabilizations on tmux 3.4, git 2.55 and the macOS runner.

## Install

```bash
npx rust-doctor@latest
```

```bash
cargo install rust-doctor
```
